independence: Authored without reading factual-grounding.ts, claim-scope.ts, new tests, runner results or parent edits for this task. Cases are newly authored and do not reuse Fieldline fixtures. The author has prior general grounding-review context from earlier tasks; this is independent of the latest implementation, not a claim of no prior exposure to the project.
scope: Expected acceptance/rejection of individual proposed review classifications, with two separate structural adversarial certificates. No API, network, database, deployment or paid calls.

contract.source: Authoritative current source. A supplied brandContext is lower-priority saved information; the current notice explicitly controls conflicts.
contract.output: Exact text whose complete meaning must be evaluated. Do not substitute a fragment that omits a qualifier or relationship.
contract.expected: allow means this text/classification or certificate may pass; reject means it must not be approved as submitted. A rejection need not discard an entire generation; repair policy is outside this fixture.
contract.kind: The submitted reviewer classification, not the author's endorsement. Rejected creative/subjective cases intentionally disguise factual claims with those labels.
contract.reason: Independent expected-judgment rationale, not a required implementation enum.
contract.evidence: Proposed exact quotes. In negative cases a quote may be real but fail entailment, omit a negation, refer to another product or represent obsolete brand data. Structural cases instead carry an explicit review certificate.
contract.positivePolicy: Supported positives are fully entailed by the supplied facts, including stated conditions and straightforward arithmetic. Creative/subjective positives make no concrete unsupported factual assertion; they need not be quoted from the source.
contract.structuralCases: evaluationLayer=review_structure requires checking the supplied units/sourceStatements/review together. Do not pass these through a text-only claim classifier and report a semantic false negative.
contract.ctaMode: Defaults to none to distinguish ordinary instructional content from engagement. The location invitation pair explicitly uses product mode, so location grounding, not CTA mode, determines its expected result.

limits: Finite synthetic expectations, not a proof of arbitrary natural-language entailment or general factual safety.
Matched positive/negative pairs share contexts and are correlated; count them as examples, not independent statistical trials.
Independent expected labels are sealed before the parent executes the validator. Do not alter them retrospectively merely to fit implementation output.
Evidence provenance, wording, scope and relations matter together; shared tokens, numerals or category names alone do not establish support.
Structural failures are reported separately from semantic false positives/negatives.
No claim is made about actual LLM semantic-review accuracy or end-to-end delivery.
